subsystems.name: Generation
subsystems.role: the source of electrical power — small nuclear fission or large sun-tracking solar.
parts: alternative: tracking solar arrays on a tall mast

subsystems.name: Storage
subsystems.role: carries the base load through lunar night and through peaks that generation alone cannot meet.

subsystems.name: Transmission network
subsystems.role: moves power from generators to every user without duplicating generators at each site.
parts: high-voltage DC cable (buried, trenched or surface-laid on posts)

subsystems.name: Power conditioning
subsystems.role: matches generator output to user equipment and isolates faults.
parts: network controller with autonomous fault isolation

subsystems.name: Thermal control
subsystems.role: keeps cables, electronics and batteries within limits across roughly 300 °C of day-night swing.
parts: radiators and heat pipes for electronics

subsystems.name: User interfaces and mobile power
subsystems.role: lets habitats, landers, rovers and processing plants plug in or carry power with them.
parts: mobile reactor sledge or battery trailer

buildSteps.title: Map the site and the loads
buildSteps.detail: Survey sunlit ridges, permanently shadowed crater floors, terrain and thermal extremes, then size the network for the habitats and processing plants it must serve.

buildSteps.title: Land the generator
buildSteps.detail: Set down a shielded fission unit at a safe distance, or erect solar arrays on a mast on a ridge where sunlight lasts almost the whole month.

buildSteps.title: Establish the main bus
buildSteps.detail: Lay a primary high-voltage DC run between the generator and the first load centre, cable on posts or in a shallow trench to limit thermal and dust damage.

buildSteps.title: Close the ring
buildSteps.detail: Wire a second route back to the source so any single cable break can be isolated without losing the whole grid; junction boxes with switchgear sit at each node.

buildSteps.title: Add storage at the nodes
buildSteps.detail: Place batteries or regenerative fuel cells where loads concentrate, so short peaks and eclipse periods are covered without oversizing the generator.

buildSteps.title: Connect the users
buildSteps.detail: Mate habitat, lander, rover and processing-plant connectors to the bus, robotically where crews are absent.

buildSteps.title: Commission and prove a lunar night
buildSteps.detail: Run the network through a full day-night cycle with autonomous fault detection, since Earth-based joystick control has a round-trip light delay of about 2.6 seconds.

buildSteps.title: Expand incrementally
buildSteps.detail: Add a second generator, more storage or a spur line to a new mining site as demand grows, rather than building one oversized plant up front.

prerequisites.why: small reactors in the tens-of-kilowatts class have been designed and studied for the Moon but none has flown or operated there.
a surface grid must hold up for roughly 14 Earth days of darkness unless it relies on nuclear heat.

prerequisites.tech: Cables and connectors for hard vacuum and thermal cycling
prerequisites.why: insulation, seals and contacts must survive vacuum, abrasive regolith dust and repeated large temperature swings.
laying and mating kilometres of conductor without crews on site has not been demonstrated on the lunar surface.
reactors, radiators and cable mass all have to be delivered to the surface in useful payload sizes.

pathway.milestone: crewed Artemis landing campaigns and small landers each carrying their own solar and battery power
pathway.unlocks: site data and experience with dust, thermal extremes and lunar night.

pathway.milestone: one fission unit in the tens-of-kilowatts class operated through a full lunar night, with a short cable run to a habitat
pathway.unlocks: proof that a shared surface grid is more mass-efficient than per-user generation.

pathway.milestone: a multi-user ring network at one polar site with storage nodes and an operating resource-processing plant on the bus
pathway.unlocks: power for oxygen extraction and other high-peak industrial loads that no single lander can supply.

pathway.milestone: an expandable, replicated polar grid with mobile power units
pathway.unlocks: interconnected habitats and industry, and a template that can be copied at other lunar sites.
